prerequisites: It is recommended to have studied Physics in the last year of high school and to have prior mathematical knowledge of vector calculus, trigonometry, and differentiation and integration of single-variable functions.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the physical-mathematical description of particle motion and know the magnitudes that quantify it.
Understand the laws and theorems that relate the motion of particles to the causes that provoke it.
Understand the concepts and principles necessary for the study of heat exchange processes in closed ideal gas systems.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbology, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and put into practice problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the course.
Acquire skills related to laboratory work and the treatment of measurements and errors.

syllabus_topics: Physical magnitudes. Treatment of measurement errors.
Thermometry and calorimetry. First principle of thermodynamics.
teaching_methods: Expository classes (Exposition and explanation of theoretical contents)
Expository classes (Evaluation activities in large groups)
Classroom practices / Seminars / Workshops (Group work activities)
Classroom practices / Seminars / Workshops (Presentation and defense of problems, assignments, projects)
Classroom practices / Seminars / Workshops (Evaluation activities in small groups)
Laboratory practices (Use of simulation software and/or experimental data processing)
Laboratory practices (Analysis of results and preparation of practice reports)
Laboratory practices (Evaluation activities in very small groups)
Problem-solving and preparation of practice reports, assignments, etc.
Use of the University of Oviedo virtual platform
assessment_rules: The final grade (NFO) is calculated as EvC + (1 – EvC/10) × CGO, where EvC is the continuous assessment grade (CPA + CCS + CPL) and CGO is the Ordinary Global Exam grade. To combine with EvC, a minimum of 3.5 points (out of 10) must be achieved in the CGO; if CGO is below 3.5, the final grade will be the CGO. A minimum overall continuous assessment score of 2.0 points (out of 5.5) is required; failure to meet this results in a continuous assessment score of zero, making the final grade equal to the CGO. A final grade below 5.0 points results in a 'Fail'; resit (extraordinary) exams carry over the EvC and apply the same calculation, with a minimum of 3.5 points in the extraordinary global exam (CGE) required for combination. Use of illicit means in any evaluable test results in a 0-Fail grade for that call.
